paragraph.text:
It starts on cron 0 5 * * * (Asia/Jerusalem), on spark.
First reads the configured sections and their search queries; then claims today's issue, unless it was already delivered.
Then searches the web for each section, for each item (up to 20).
Each time, from here on, only if deliver is true, runs the section's web search, trying up to 3 times; then keeps only the results the issue may show.
Then summarises each section, for each item (up to 20).
Each time, if deliver is true and results is not {}, asks the language model for a short summary of the section's results, trying up to 2 times, carrying on even if it fails.
Then, if deliver is true, check the summary, carrying on even if it fails.
Then, if deliver is true, renders the issue as an email and as an EPUB; then checks the email has not been sent yet and freezes what will be sent.
Then, if send is true, sends the issue by email, trying up to 3 times, carrying on even if it fails.
Then, if deliver is true, records the sent email and checks the reader does not have the issue yet.
Then, if deliver is true and push is true, queues the EPUB on the e-reader, trying up to 3 times.
Then, if deliver is true, marks the day's issue as delivered.
Nothing continues from here.
When it is done, nothing else happens.

daily-newspaper.notes: #53: one dated issue a day. Parse the sections, claim the local date (a date already delivered ends the run with nothing sent), search and filter each section, summarise it with cortex until the summary window closes (a failed or late summary leaves the results-only rendering), render the HTML and the EPUB, then deliver behind lease fences: the email (once per date, with a durable per-date key and the first rendered payload), the push to the library, the delivery record. Non-agentic: no bridge actor, no agent step.

repodocs-sync.description: Pushes the specs, plans, delivery summaries, designs and devague files of every repo on this machine to the library, sending only what changed since the last run.
repodocs-sync.name: Push repo documents to the library
repodocs-sync.notes: One repodocs.sync step through culture-library-repodocs: every top-level repo under the actor's repos_root, each file's default-branch version, its working draft when it differs, tombstones for vanished files and spec links (docs/operations/repodocs.md). It outputs counts only.

steps.description: Sends each changed file, draft and deletion to the library and counts them.
steps.name: Push what changed
steps.notes: repodocs.sync: stops at the actor's max_seconds (300) and the next run resumes from the state file; per-file errors are counted, never fatal. timeout_s leaves room beyond max_seconds.

transcribe-file.description: Turns one audio file into a transcript file with timestamps. Running it again on the same audio and model changes nothing; another model writes a second file beside the first.

inputs.description: the audio file's absolute path, under the actor's audio_root
inputs.name: audio_path

inputs.description: the audio file's sha256: 64 lowercase hex characters
inputs.name: audio_sha256

inputs.description: a language code such as he or en; unset: the endpoint's default
inputs.name: language

inputs.description: the model to label and ask for; unset: the actor's model
inputs.name: model

inputs.description: the directory the transcript goes under, inside the actor's output_root
inputs.name: output_dir

inputs.description: when the recording was made, ISO-8601 UTC; passed through
inputs.name: recorded_at

transcribe-file.name: Transcribe an audio file
transcribe-file.notes: File in, file out: one audio.transcribe step. The transcript is written atomically to <output_dir>/<audio_sha256>/transcript.<model-slug>.json (schema 1: audio_sha256, model, language, duration, segments [{start, end, text}], created_at, window_count, empty_window_count); the outputs carry only scalars, never the text. Re-running the same audio and model is a no-op; another model writes a second file beside the first. The workflow knows nothing about where the file came from.

steps.description: Sends the audio to the speech-to-text actor and writes the transcript.

inputs.description: the audio file's absolute path, under the actor's audio_root
inputs.name: audio_path

inputs.description: the audio file's sha256: 64 lowercase hex characters
inputs.name: audio_sha256

inputs.description: a language code such as he or en; unset: the endpoint's default
inputs.name: language

inputs.description: the model to label and ask for; unset: the actor's model
inputs.name: model

inputs.description: the directory the transcript goes under, inside the actor's output_root
inputs.name: output_dir

steps.name: Transcribe the file
steps.notes: audio.transcribe through stt-en. Checks audio_sha256 (64 hex), keeps audio_path under the actor's audio_root and output_dir under its output_root (path_refused), hashes the file (audio_mismatch), and returns the existing <output_dir>/<audio_sha256>/transcript.<model-slug>.json unchanged when its audio_sha256 and model match (no request). Otherwise ffmpeg cuts 16 kHz mono WAV windows of at most 480 s (at a silence in a window's last 60 s when there is one), each POSTed to <base_url>/v1/audio/transcriptions; each reply is kept under .work.<model-slug>/ so a retry resends only the missing windows. timeout_s 14400 covers a 3.8 h recording (the engine default is 3600 s); only stt_unavailable is retried.

outputs.description: the transcript file's absolute path
outputs.name: result_path

outputs.description: the sha256 of the transcript file's bytes
outputs.name: result_sha256

outputs.description: the sha256 of the audio that was transcribed
outputs.name: audio_sha256

outputs.description: the model the transcript is labelled with
outputs.name: model

outputs.description: the language sent, or null
outputs.name: language

outputs.description: how many segments the transcript has
outputs.name: segment_count

outputs.description: how many windows the audio was cut into
outputs.name: window_count

outputs.description: how many windows came back with no text
outputs.name: empty_window_count

transcript-to-reader.description: Turns one finished transcript into a book on the e-reader: a short summary first, then the transcript. Running it again on the same transcript adds no second copy.

inputs.description: the finished transcript's absolute path
inputs.name: result_path

inputs.description: the recording's audio file, for the fallback
inputs.name: audio_path

inputs.description: the recording's sha256
inputs.name: audio_sha256

inputs.description: the transcripts root the transcript is under
inputs.name: output_dir

inputs.description: when Pocket recorded it, ISO-8601 UTC
inputs.name: recorded_at

inputs.description: the recording's language code, if any
inputs.name: language

inputs.description: the finished run's window count
inputs.name: window_count

inputs.description: how many of those windows came back empty
inputs.name: empty_window_count

inputs.description: the device to queue on (newspaper_device), used only when the library actor has a queue_path; unset: the actor's device_id
inputs.name: device_id

transcript-to-reader.name: Put a transcript on the reader
transcript-to-reader.notes: One book per recording, after its transcription finishes (fired by the transcription run's rules.run.succeeded, rule pocket-to-reader). An en recording whose whisper windows were all empty is first transcribed again on stt-he (fallback; keep and pick choose the transcript). Then a 1-2 line summary on cortex-spark2 that reads the transcript itself (d2), the EPUB, and the push to the reader. Outputs carry no transcript or summary text.

steps.description: Transcribes the audio again with the Hebrew model when the English transcript came back empty.
steps.name: Transcribe again in Hebrew
steps.notes: q1: only for an en recording whose whisper windows all came back empty (empty_window_count == window_count): audio.transcribe through stt-he writes the zipformer transcript beside whisper's, and the book uses it. Otherwise skipped.

outputs.description: the zipformer transcript's absolute path
outputs.name: result_path

steps.description: Keeps the finished transcript when no second transcription is needed.
steps.name: Keep the finished transcript
steps.notes: select over the one given path: passes the finished run's transcript through, skipped exactly when fallback runs, so pick sees one path.

steps.description: Picks the transcript the book is made from.
steps.name: Pick the transcript
steps.notes: select: the transcript the book is made from, from whichever of fallback or keep ran.

steps.description: Asks the language model for a one- or two-line summary and a one-word topic.
steps.name: Summarise the recording
steps.notes: llm.complete on cortex-spark2 with the brief named transcript (the actor's params.briefs): it reads the first 48000 characters of the transcript itself (content_path, d2), so the transcript text never enters the run; the reply is JSON {summary, word}. on_error skip: the book still ships, titled <date> <HHMM> recording, with "Summary unavailable." (that book is not kept, so a later run with a summary replaces it).

steps.description: Makes the book, titled with the recording's date and topic, right to left for Hebrew.
steps.name: Make the book
steps.notes: transcript.render: one EPUB, titled <YYYY-MM-DD> <HHMM> <word> (the Asia/Jerusalem date and time of recorded_at), the summary then the transcript; right to left unless the language is en. The same inputs give the same bytes, so a repeat is deduplicated by the library.

steps.description: Uploads the book to the e-reader library and queues it for the device.
steps.name: Put the book in the library
steps.notes: library.push through newspaper-library: upload the book as kind transcript, visibility private (recordings are personal). The library and what it accepts are the actor's params (culture-rules#86); the device_id input is used only when the actor has a queue_path. Uploading the same bytes again returns the existing item (created false).
